answer: The protocol mandates 3,000 megabytes of memory-hard work per node to gate access, where a verifier tracks each agent as a glowing ember of active state within the network heap. Each instance must maintain an exclusive memory-resident table that acts as a beacon to detect overlapping compute signatures; any failure to clear this space between tasks results in immediate evidence of shared resource usage. An honest agent pays for one unit of cost, while 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost, forcing attackers to forge multiple isolated memory paths or risk permanent slashing.
